page: Amazon Web Services c8id.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

For local storage, the instance includes 2850 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a 22 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In benchmark evaluations, the c8id.12xlarge demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, reaching 3859.38 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 194.95 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Compute performance is highlighted by a Passmark CPU score of 69,316.76 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 19,875.0. It also shows top-tier performance in image processing and text processing workloads.

The hardware configuration is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that require fast local scratch space. However, the compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for memory-bound applications. The inclusion of AMX instructions enables efficient CPU-based machine learning tasks, as evidenced by LLM prompt processing speeds of 254.3 tokens/sec on a 7B model. The combination of high-speed DDR5 memory, dedicated CPU allocation, and local NVMe storage makes the c8id.12xlarge appropriate for software compilation, database operations, high-throughput web serving, and data decompression pipelines.
